segments.title: 第63章 軍訓結束
segments.content:
Reigniting the Prime of Youth Chapter 63: The End of Military Training

If any other ordinary girls had been present, Zhu Yufei and the others could have continued to jeer and laugh their heads off.

But it was Ying Chanxi who had appeared. A girl who possessed both beauty and the status of a top student, she exuded an indefinable aura even when just walking down a path.

Her presence instantly silenced Zhu Yufei, Lin Yuan, and the others, who obediently stepped aside to watch the show.

As for Li Luo, he looked at Ying Chanxi, then at the two bottles of water in her hand, and raised an eyebrow, shamelessly extending his hand. "You can't finish both of these, right? Let me help you with one."

"In your dreams," Ying Chanxi huffed, twisting her body to dodge his thieving hand and protect the two bottles. "You're so capable now, so popular. From now on, you should drink the beverages other girls give you."

"But I don't drink sodas." Li Luo handed over the Coke in his hand, pushing it into Ying Chanxi's arms, and forcibly snatched one of her water bottles. "I need to lose weight lately, so water is healthier. You can take care of this soda for me."

Qiao Xinyan, who was watching the show from the side, blinked. She felt that this excuse sounded a bit familiar and took a couple more glances at Ying Chanxi.

"How much do you even weigh to be losing weight? Only a fool would believe you..." Ying Chanxi muttered, but her hand clutching the Coke showed no sign of letting go. "Besides, isn't it a bit wrong for you to give me a drink someone else gave you?"

"I'm not obligated to manage the feelings of every girl who has a crush on me." Li Luo twisted open the water Ying Chanxi had given him and took two big gulps. "Otherwise, wouldn't I be busy to death for all three years of high school?"

"Shameless," Ying Chanxi rolled her eyes at him, then said, "I have my own water. You should keep this soda for yourself."

"I have water too." Li Luo shook the bottle in his hand, then pointed to Yan Zhusheng under the shade of a tree not far away. "If you can't finish it, go offer it to her."

"Huh?" Ying Chanxi was taken aback for a moment and couldn't help but walk toward Yan Zhusheng.

Yan Zhusheng was sitting on a bench, gently strumming the guitar in her arms.

Her eyes were closed in deep concentration, humming a tune, completely unaware of the surrounding students who had gathered to watch.

Next to her and at her feet, there were already eight or nine bottles of various beverages, all given by boys who had mustered up the courage to do so.

Ever since Yan Zhusheng had shown off her singing voice on the athletic field last night, many people had started asking about her.

When they came to see what she looked like during the day, they were utterly stunned by her beauty.

And just like that, Yan Zhusheng became a hot topic in the gossip circles of every class, much like Ying Chanxi had during the summer preparatory classes.

Some of the bolder boys were already sending signals of affection toward Yan Zhusheng.

However, Yan Zhusheng was completely oblivious to all this. After finishing her song, she opened her eyes and returned to her cool and aloof state.

She glanced down at the drinks on the ground, silently picked them up, and then walked over to Li Luo and the others. "Do you guys want some? I can't finish them all."

"See?" Li Luo glanced at Ying Chanxi. "They're all drinks given by others, but aren't they just given to someone else in the end? The drinks other boys gave you in middle school, didn't they all end up in my stomach?"

Zhu Yufei, Lin Yuan, and the others ran over cheering, picking out drinks from Yan Zhusheng's hands and shouting "Hooray!"

Ying Chanxi just rolled her eyes at him, silently put away the Coke in her hand, and couldn't be bothered with him anymore. She walked over to Yan Zhusheng and asked, "Want to go for a walk together?"

After handing out the drinks, Yan Zhusheng turned to look at Ying Chanxi, thought for a moment, and then nodded. "Okay."

...

At ten o'clock at night, the lights in the dormitory building went out.

Early the next morning, before six, the chief instructor's whistle sounded from downstairs.

The military training at the barracks officially began.

They had originally thought the training intensity would be higher at the military base.

But to Li Luo's surprise, they mainly practiced standing at attention and goose-stepping in the morning, while the afternoons were filled with all sorts of interesting activities.

Thursday was obstacle course training, with competitions between classes for the fastest time. Watching the instructors' demonstrations, they all ran incredibly fast, scaling walls as easily as getting into bed.

But when they had to run it themselves, one after another, they all made fools of themselves.

Friday was firearms experience. Unfortunately, each person was only allotted three bullets, so it was just a brief taste before they were ushered away.

Still, to be able to touch a real gun in his lifetime, Li Luo could only say that First Affiliated High was truly on another level; even the military training treatment was different.

His high school military training in his past life had just been for show, and it was even more perfunctory in vocational college. How could it compare to the fun of being in a real military camp?

He used to think that top students were all bookworms. Now that he was at First Affiliated High, he realized that damn, the lives of top students were truly different—exciting and rich. His past self was such a huge idiot.

By Saturday afternoon, they had arranged an outdoor exploration activity.

The instructors marked out a large area on the mountain behind the barracks and led them on a training march for several kilometers.

They also taught them how to properly set up a camp and start a fire in the mountains.

On Sunday morning, it was time to review the results of the military training.

Each class marched in formation past the reviewing stand, followed by the tedious wait for the leaders to finish their speeches.

After their last lunch in the barracks, everyone reluctantly boarded the bus back to school.

"I have some good news and some bad news," Kong Junxiang said with a smile on the bus, taking advantage of the fact that everyone was still awake right after the bus started moving.

"Teacher Kong, tell us the good news first," Zhu Yufei said loudly. "After the good news, I'll go right to sleep. Let them listen to the bad news."

"The good news," Kong Junxiang cleared his throat, "is that after we get back to school, the first-year students will be on break immediately. You don't need to come too early tomorrow morning, just be at school by eight."

"Then what's the bad news?"

"The bad news," Kong Junxiang smiled, "is that tomorrow and the day after are the placement exams for the start of the school year. But don't be nervous, just relax. It's just to get a general idea of your current level."

As soon as he said this, the bus was filled with wails of despair.

Li Luo also sighed.

There was no way to know the questions on this test in advance. His score probably wouldn't be very good.

However, he wasn't in a hurry to get good grades right away. It was a rare second chance at life, and there was still plenty of time in high school for him to study hard.

...

The bus drove into the school.

The students returned to their classroom, packed up their things briefly, and then scattered.

Li Luo stayed behind in the classroom to arrange for the other three class committee members to help set up the desks and chairs for the exam.

In the middle of it all, Ying Chanxi came downstairs to find Li Luo. "I'm going out with Xinyan this afternoon. Are you coming?"

"You guys go ahead. I'm exhausted, I need to go back and rest," Li Luo said, waving his hand.

His novel had already been running on its stockpile for seven days. Although a stockpile of 250,000 words was a lot, it couldn't last forever.

Especially since his scheduled releases these past few days were ten thousand words daily, the rate of consumption was not slow.

It would be better to go back and write for a while.

Seeing that he wasn't going to hang out with them, Ying Chanxi huffed and turned to leave.

Li Luo had also planned to leave as soon as the classroom was set up. Before he left, he took out his phone, opened the Qidian Reading app, and glanced at his book's review section.

The next moment, he froze.

"What the heck is 'Annual Rings'? I searched for it, and there's no such song. Could it be an original by the author?"
